subject: Intermittent 502s on large POSTs after private cutover - NAT/MTU investigation
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@bluewave.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent API 502s after private cutover

Hi Priya,

We cut over BlueWave's private deployment to Redwood Private earlier this morning. Since then we've seen intermittent 502 responses from our ingress (API gateway) for large POST requests (payloads ~12-16 KB). The errors spike under concurrent upload load (50-200 concurrent clients) and typically affect requests that are not retried quickly.

What we've observed:
- 502/Bad Gateway returned from our front proxy; backend service shows no application error.
- Packet captures on our gateway show a mix of RSTs and ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages to internal hosts (we suspect PMTUD or MTU blackhole).
- Flow logs show a high number of ephemeral source port reuse / short-lived translations during the spikes; our NAT pool is configured to use a limited SNAT range for the outbound path to Redwood edge.

We need Redwood support to triage routing/NAT/MTU interaction — this looks like a combination of large payload path MTU and SNAT port exhaustion under concurrency, but can't be sure. I've attached a tcpdump and flow log snippet.

Attachments: bluewave_tcpdump_20260218.pcap, flow_logs_20260218.txt

Can someone from networking take a look and advise immediate mitigations? We're seeing customer impact during peak ingest windows.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer
BlueWave

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@bluewave.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent API 502s after private cutover

Hi Julia — thanks for the data, and sorry you're seeing this. I've started digging in; initial ask below so we can narrow root cause quickly.

Can you please provide:
- Exact timestamps (UTC) for 3 representative failed requests (include request IDs if available).
- The full NAT config snippet for the SNAT pool (you attached a cropped view; we need the exact port range and mapping policy).
- tcpdump pcap + a short text extract (tcpdump -n -r) for the window around failures (you attached, good).
- Output of: `sudo sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing`, `ip addr show` on the gateway, `iptables -t nat -L -n -v` (or the platform equivalent).
- Any asymmetric routing indication (do your upstreams show replies coming back via a different hop?).
- Kernel dmesg around the spike timeframe (any ICMP PMTU messages logged?)
- If possible, a short load test run (iperf or simple curl loop) to reproduce while we watch counters.

Immediate mitigations we can consider while diagnosing:
1) Temporarily expand your SNAT port range / use additional ephemeral pool on the outbound path to increase available translations.
2) If asymmetric routing is present, ensure conntrack timeouts are conservative or configure NAT persistence for the service VIP (1:1 SNAT where possible).
3) On the gateway, enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 and/or set MSS clamping on the path to Redwood edge as a quick test.

I'm looping in Marissa (network) and Markus (infra) to help validate on the Redwood side.

I'll review the pcap now and follow up with a concrete triage play.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Solutions Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 07:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent API 502s after private cutover

Hi Priya,

Thanks — added the extra artifacts. Here are the additional details you requested:
- Representative failed request IDs (UTC): 2026-02-18T16:22:03Z (req-84f2), 2026-02-18T16:23:11Z (req-84f9), 2026-02-18T16:31:47Z (req-8512).
- NAT config: SNAT pool on our edge is using source ports 40000-60999 (port range 20999 ports). We do port-preserving for the majority of flows. I've included nat_config_snippet.txt.
- tcpdump extract: during the spike we see repeated SYN/ACKs, then a rapid sequence of RSTs from our gateway toward the client IPs. Also, ICMP Type 3 Code 4 (fragmentation needed) is seen with mtu=1436 toward the backend VIP IPs.
- No obvious asymmetric routing from our side; traceroutes from the gateway to Redwood edge show a stable 3-hop path. However, packet captures at our gateway and at the client-facing load balancer show different egress IPs during the event.
- dmesg has occasional entries showing "IP fragmentation needed and DF set" for connections to the VIP.

We uploaded the full pcap to: https://s3.amazonaws.com/bluewave-share/tcpdump_20260218.pcap

Let us know the next steps and if you need us to run any changes on our side.

— BlueWave Ops (Julia)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Julia Park <julia.park@bluewave.com>, ops@bluewave.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent API 502s after private cutover — initial triage and recommended mitigations

Marissa / Markus — forwarding BlueWave's packet captures and config. Summary of my read after a quick pass on the pcap:

Key observations:
- ICMP "fragmentation needed" with mtu=1436 toward the backend VIP. That suggests PMTUD failing on the path (likely an MTU < 1500 hop — could be tunnel/encap between BlueWave and Redwood edge).
- Simultaneous high concurrency of large POSTs combined with short SNAT port range can lead to port reuse and early connection teardown when ephemeral ports are exhausted (we see a lot of FIN/RST sequences from the gateway).
- The traces show some requests where the SYN reached Redwood edge but the server's SYN/ACK is not received by the client due to the ICMP MTU issue and then the gateway tears down the flow.

Proposed immediate mitigations (low-risk first):
1) Ask BlueWave to temporarily enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 on gateway and add MSS clamping to 1400 on paths to the Redwood edge (this will avoid PMTUD blackhole while we find the encap MTU).
2) Request BlueWave expand SNAT ephemeral range (e.g., add 20000 ports or allocate a second SNAT public IP block) to reduce port collision under concurrency.
3) On Redwood side, enable logging for asymmetric path detection and keep a short-lived pinning (sticky SNAT) for flows from BlueWave to reduce translation churn.
4) If traffic still fails, propose switching the product ingress to use a dedicated 1:1 SNAT mapping for the service VIP as a short-term fix.

If both agree, we can coordinate a maintenance window tonight (US west) to apply items 1 and 2 and monitor for improvement.

Next steps: Julia — can you confirm willingness to: A) do tcp_mtu_probing/MSS clamp trial, B) expand SNAT port range (or add a second SNAT IP) tonight? Also provide a window you prefer (we can do 21:00-23:00 PST tonight).

— Priya

From: Julia Park <julia.park@bluewave.com>

Hi Priya / Marissa / Markus — thanks for the quick analysis and suggested actions.

We will:
- Enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 and apply MSS clamp to 1400 on the gateway at 21:00 PST tonight.
- Expand our SNAT port range by assigning an additional public SNAT IP (doubling available ports) at the same maintenance window.
- We'll run a synthetic load (50-200 concurrent clients with 12–16 KB payloads) during and after the change and upload the results to the S3 share for you to review.

I'll create a short runbook of commands we'll execute and post the link to the shared S3 when done. If you can monitor from the Redwood edge and confirm whether the ICMP PMTU messages disappear after the MSS clamp, that would be ideal.

Attachments: nat_config_snippet.txt

Thanks — Julia
